text.p: Austrian national grid company Verbund said on Thursday it expected a slight increase in 1996 earnings, helped by the reduction of provisions for fluctuations of the Swiss franc against the schilling.

"We were able to draw on provisions totaling about 700 million schillings," finance chief Michael Pistauer told an investors' conference, adding that the weaker franc should help improve the group's financial result.
Verbund allocated 643.4 million schillings to provisions for foreign currency liabilities in 1995 alone. More than a quarter of its 42 billion schillings in liabilities are denominated in francs.

Verbund, which supplies about two thirds of Austria's electricity needs, in 1995 reported a pre-tax profit of 1.41 billion schillings and net earnings of 1.38 billion on electricity sales of 19.6 billion schillings.
Pistauer said lower river water levels, which forced the company to turn from cheap hydro electricity to thermal power, had weighed on last year's earnings.
"The result was affected by higher fuel costs. Production at our hydro power plants was poor due to low water levels in the first nine months of the year", he said.

Verbund, faced with the gradual opening of national energy markets over the next few years in line with European Union directives, was determined to power on with its restructuring and cost savings programme, Pistauer said.

The company wants to cut costs by about one billion schillings annually until the beginning of the next decade. Pistauer said Verbund planned to reduce its 4,650 strong workforce by about 200 in both this and next year. -- Christian Gutlederer, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
